newsitem.title: HONG KONG: HK Building loan raised to HK$1.2 bln.
newsitem.headline: HK Building loan raised to HK$1.2 bln.

text.p: Hong Kong Building and Loan Agency's loan facility has been raised to HK$1.2 billion from HK$1 billion, arranger Schroders Asia said on Tuesday.
Bankers said the bullet loan has a tenor of three years. It pays an interest margin of 150 basis points over the Hong Kong Interbank Offered Rate.

Fees are 52.5 basis points for co-arrangers committing HK$100 million, 30 basis points for senior managers committing HK$50 million, and 25 basis points for managers committing HK$30 million, bankers noted.
The deal is secured over residential mortgages in Hong Kong.
The borrower is 41.46 percent held by China Resources Holdings.
A total of 21 financial institutions joined the syndication.
Co-arrangers are Bank Austria Aktiengesellschaft, Hong Kong, Bank of Nova Scotia, Bank of Scotland, Sin Hua Bank and WestLB.
Senior Managers are BHF-Bank, NM Rothschild and Sons HK, Daiwa Bank, Emirates Bank International PJSC, Industrial Bank of Japan, RaboBank, Seng Heng Bank and Tai Fung Bank.
Managers are Banco Delta Asia, Bayerische Vereinsbank Hong Kong, GE Capital Finance, Fuji Bank, Tat Lee Bank, Thai Farmers Bank and Bank of Tokyo-Mitsuibishi
